dedupe_keys.name: a high precision catalogue of landslide events in china based on news text mining with large language model

description: A high-precision catalogue of landslide events in China based on news text mining with large language model is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Binru Zhao et al. Landslides are a major geological hazard causing significant casualties and economic losses. Reliable risk assessment requires high-quality spatiotemporal event data, yet no publicly available landslide catalogue with fine-grained precision exists for China. To address this, we developed a landslide event catalogue for mainland China from 2008–2024 based on news reports. Coverage: national (CN); published in 2026. Formats: Excel. The data are held in Figshare and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 842844 Bytes. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support industrial-facility and resource studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
